disclosure: Every rule below is deterministic and disclosed here. Fills are SIMULATED (no orders are ever placed). All inputs come from the official Kalshi demo Trade API public endpoints; nothing is inferred or fabricated. If a required input is missing, the trade is skipped and the reason is logged in run_log.json.
started_cash_note: Simulated starting bankroll in demo dollars. Not real money, not an official Kalshi balance.

universe.notional_basis: computed 24h traded notional = volume_24h_fp x last_price_dollars (both official market fields). 'Highest dollar amount' is not an official Kalshi field; this is a disclosed estimate, not an official metric.
universe.coverage: General scan paginates GET /markets?status=open (sort order is not guaranteed by the API, so it may miss sparse series). The documented series_ticker filter then targets the demo series observed to carry the tracked topics' open lineups (config topics.known_series; membership comes from this repo's verified demo snapshots, and each query is logged with its URL). A series with no open markets simply returns an empty page.
universe.volume_floor_note: The demo exchange is extremely thin: most markets trade 0 contracts in 24h (flagged irregularity across sessions). The floor is 5 contracts, far below any production-equivalent threshold.

topics.note: First matching rule wins; classification is by series/event ticker and title keywords. Official series category strings for the demo exchange are not published; keyword matching is disclosed per row via matched_by.
topics.known_series_note: Demo series observed in this repo's verified snapshots (data/demo-snapshot.json categories; strategy-desk series map). Series with no open markets return an empty page and are logged.

signal_source: Public trades tape: GET /markets/trades?ticker=<market>&limit=200 (official public endpoint), sorted by created_time ascending. The demo candlesticks endpoint currently returns empty arrays for most markets even when trades occurred minutes earlier — captured and flagged by this repo's other desks (decision/data/snapshot-orderbook-candlesticks.json; docs/data/history.json: 15/15 markets with zero candles) — so signals run on executed-trade prices, not candles. Trades tape thresholds are matched to demo reality: most candidate markets execute only a handful of trades per 24h (volume counts CONTRACTS, not trades).

strategies.name: momentum-tape
strategies.desc: If the YES trade-price trend over the recent tape (last trade minus the trade 6 trades back) is >= +$0.05, buy YES; if <= -$0.05, buy NO. Entry only if the implied ask of that side is within the entry band.
strategies.min_trades_note: needs a 6-trade window; markets with fewer trades only qualify for mean-revert/longshot

strategies.name: mean-revert-tape
strategies.desc: If the last trade price deviates from the mean of the most recent 20 trades (minimum 6) by <= -$0.10, buy YES (fade the drop); if >= +$0.10, buy NO (fade the rise). Entry only if the implied ask of that side is within the entry band.

strategies.name: longshot-value
strategies.desc: If the implied NO ask is <= $0.20 and the market traded >= 500 contracts in 24h, buy NO. Runs only when no other strategy fired on that market. (Floor lowered from the production-scale 5000 to match the demo exchange's thin books — disclosed.)

fill_rule.entry_price: implied best ask of the bought side = 1.00 - best bid of the opposite side (official rule from docs.kalshi.com/getting_started/orderbook_responses: a NO bid at Y equals a YES ask at $1.00 - Y). Simulated as an immediately-matched (taker) fill, so the official taker fee applies.
fill_rule.limitations: The REST book lists bids only, so ask-side depth is implied, not observed. A simulated fill does not move the market and may not be achievable in real size. Demo books are thin (official demo-environment warning).

fee_rule.formula: fee = roundup(M x 0.07 x C x P x (1-P)), M = 1
fee_rule.multiplier_note: Taker multiplier M=1 is confirmed for KXAAAGASM (gas) and KXBTCMAX150 (crypto) in the official non-standard-fee table; the full table's other rows are not machine-readable from the PDF (flagged IR), so M=1 is assumed and disclosed for all simulated trades.

mark_rule: Open positions are marked to market with the official last_price_dollars field (held-side value = last YES price for YES, 1 - last YES price for NO). Marks are last-trade based and can lag the book (official responses-cached caveat).
settlement_rule: When a market with an open simulated position reports a settled status (status in {settled, finalized} — the demo exchange has returned both spellings, a flagged demo-vs-docs enum irregularity) and result in {yes,no}: payout = $1.00 per contract if the held side matches result, else $0.00 (official market-settlement rule). Settlement fee = $0 for simple yes/no determinations (official fee schedule).

api_politeness.note: Unauthenticated public market data; rate limits per docs.kalshi.com/getting_started/rate_limits (10 tokens/request default). Call budget per run is bounded by candidates_max.
